# OpenRouter Reasoning Tokens & `max_tokens` Interaction

## The primary source: OpenRouter's official docs

Yes — OpenRouter has published official documentation on this topic. The relevant page is their **Reasoning Tokens** documentation.

> "The `max_tokens` parameter includes both reasoning tokens and visible output tokens. If you set `max_tokens` to 1000 and the model uses 800 tokens for reasoning, you'll only receive 200 tokens of visible output."

— [openrouter.ai/docs](https://openrouter.ai/docs/use-cases/reasoning-tokens)

The documentation recommends one of two approaches to avoid the reasoning eating into the visible output budget:

> "To ensure you receive your desired amount of visible output, you can either set a higher `max_tokens` value or use the `reasoning.max_tokens` parameter to explicitly control the reasoning budget separately."

— [openrouter.ai/docs](https://openrouter.ai/docs/use-cases/reasoning-tokens)

The docs describe a `reasoning` parameter object that can be passed in the request body:

> "You can control reasoning behavior using the `reasoning` parameter in your request. This parameter accepts an object with `effort` (for models that support effort levels like 'low', 'medium', 'high') or `max_tokens` (to set a specific token budget for reasoning)."

— [openrouter.ai/docs](https://openrouter.ai/docs/use-cases/reasoning-tokens)

## Summary of the documented behavior

Per the official docs:

1. **`max_tokens` is a combined budget.** It caps reasoning tokens + output tokens together by default.
2. **You can separate them.** Setting `reasoning.max_tokens` allocates a specific budget for reasoning, which then doesn't consume from the main `max_tokens` pool for visible output.
3. **Some models support `reasoning.effort`** instead of (or alongside) an explicit token count.

## What I did *not* verify

- **Per-model behavior differences.** The docs indicate the `reasoning` parameter is model-dependent ("for models that support effort levels"), but I did not verify which specific models accept `effort` vs. `max_tokens` vs. both. That information may be on individual model pages on OpenRouter, but I did not retrieve those.
- **Exact edge-case behavior.** For example, what happens if you set `max_tokens: 500` and `reasoning.max_tokens: 400` — whether the visible output is hard-capped at 100, or whether the API returns an error or clamps differently. The docs describe the general principle but I did not find explicit documentation of every edge case.
- **Whether this behavior has changed over time.** I am citing the documentation as it currently exists. I cannot speak to earlier versions of the docs or whether the behavior was different at launch.

If any of those gaps matter for your use case, let me know and I can try to dig into the specific model pages or API reference.
